//: Lighthouse CI for the FSA Normal Grazing Periods map. staticDistDir is deliberately NOT used: it serves the given directory at the server ROOT, and this app deploys under /lfp-explorer/ — a root-served copy resolves brand/site.webmanifest and assets/*.json fine but changes the geometry every other tool here audits, and the meta CSP's 'self' would then mean a different origin path. So collect.url points at a server the caller must already have running. Bring it up over the WORKSPACE root, not the repo: python3 -m http.server 8000 -d /path/to/sustainable-fsa   then: npx --prefix tools lhci autorun --config=.lighthouserc.json

settings.//: The app's own boot marker (dataset.ngpReady) is the render gate everywhere else in this suite; Lighthouse cannot read it, so it gets a generous fixed wait instead. maxWaitForLoad covers the 5.1 MB local payload plus the county geometry, range-requested live from data.sustainable-fsa.com: a 63 KB (brotli) index sidecar plus the PMTiles reads for the fit view, about 348 KB all in. That REPLACED a 453 KB brotli TopoJSON, so the boundary bytes went DOWN — but it is now two origins and a range-request pattern instead of one file, which is why the wait stays generous.

assert.//: NO COMMENT KEY BELOW. Every key inside `assertions` is read as an audit or category id, and a "//" there fails the run with '"//" is not a known audit'. Accessibility is the hard gate: axe over six interaction states already passes at zero serious/critical, so a Lighthouse a11y score under 1.0 means something the interaction audit cannot see. Best-practices is an error too. Performance is a WARNING on purpose — the page ships a 5 MB JSON payload and range-requests a PMTiles county archive over the network by design, and under Lighthouse's simulated mobile throttling that lands around 0.3. The boundary bytes went DOWN at the tiled cut-over (453 KB brotli TopoJSON to ~348 KB of sidecar plus tiles) while the request COUNT went up, so the score has to be re-measured rather than assumed to have moved either way. Treat the number as a trend line, not a gate; the fix is a payload change, not a threshold change.
